# tellmewhy

> A private place to talk about how you feel. Message an AI that answers now, and — if you ever want one — a single trusted person who reads only what you choose to share.

tellmewhy is a mobile-first web app for talking through your feelings with an AI. You can organize conversations into folders and, optionally, link one trusted person (a therapist or anyone else) who reads only the conversations you actively share.

## Privacy model

- Message bodies, conversation titles, and folder names are encrypted at rest with a key that is yours. A database breach or backup leak exposes no content — only metadata (when conversations happened, which messages were crisis-flagged, who is linked to whom).
- It is NOT end-to-end encrypted. The AI has to read your words to reply, so plaintext briefly exists in server memory during inference; it is discarded the moment the reply is done, and only the encrypted version is ever stored. The encryption protects against database breaches, not against the processing that makes a reply possible.
- Nothing is shared by default. You share one conversation at a time and can revoke any share instantly — past and future messages alike.
- AI calls route through OpenRouter with per-request data collection denied, and the account is restricted to providers that don't log or train on inputs. Your conversations are used to write you a reply and nothing else.
- Deleting your account is self-serve from `/account` (password + acknowledgment): in one transaction your encryption key is crypto-shredded — nothing encrypted can ever be read again, by anyone, including us — and every row you own is purged, ending all sessions. What remains by design: audit lines of ids and times (no content), and, if you'd linked a trusted person, the notes they wrote (their key, their record) plus a name-only departure marker.
- Forgot your password? Reset it by email. It restores access only — your key is wrapped by the server, not your password, so a reset never decrypts or exposes content to anyone; the email is a link and nothing else, responses don't reveal whether an address has an account, and all other sessions end on reset. Email is not verified at sign-up.
- Page views are counted with a self-hosted, cookieless analytics instance (Umami) on our own infrastructure: paths and visit metadata only — no cookies, no third party, never message content.

## What it is not

- Not a medical device, and not a substitute for professional care or emergency services.
- Not a crisis service. If it detects a crisis signal it surfaces hotline resources (988 in the US, findahelpline.com internationally) and flags the message for a trusted person's attention queue in the conversations you've shared — it does not push an alert. In an emergency, contact your local emergency services.
